items.name: Perfectly Pretty Hotcakes
ingredients: 2 tbsp melted butter, plus extra for frying
Butter or whipped cream, to serve
steps: Add the lemon juice to a non-metallic bowl, pour in the milk and whisk to combine. Leave to sit for 5 minutes to curdle.
Sift the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt into another bowl and whisk to combine evenly.
Beat the eggs and sugar until thick and pale, then beat in the melted butter.
Make a well in the dry ingredients, add the egg mixture, soured milk and vanilla, and whisk gently from the centre until smooth.
Heat a large non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat. To test, flick a few drops of water in — they should dance. Add a little butter if needed, and cook a small sacrificial hotcake first.
Cook each hotcake for a minute or so until bubbles form and pop, then flip and cook through until golden on both sides.
Serve with lashings of maple syrup and butter or cream.

items.name: Booth's Ginger Crunch
items.desc: Base doubled and icing tripled from the original recipe.

items.name: B's Dope-As Brownie
steps: Melt the butter and chocolate in a pot, then take off the heat and stir in the sugar and eggs. Mix in all the dry ingredients.
Optional toppings — anything goes, but Whittaker's creamy caramel poked in is good, as is Nestlé tinned caramel, raspberries, etc.
Best cooked in a cast-iron dish, or doubled in a baking pan.
Bake at 170°C for about 22 minutes.

items.name: Chocolate Chewy Cookies
steps: Mix into a dough and roll into balls.
Bake for 15 minutes at 170°C.

items.name: Gingerbread Cookies
steps: Cream together the butter and brown sugar.
Add the ginger, cinnamon and mixed spice.
Mix in the eggs and golden syrup.
Slowly add the flour, baking powder and baking soda.
Chill in cling film for 30 minutes.
Roll out to about 4–5mm and cut.
Chill in the fridge for 5–10 minutes.
Bake on the pizza setting for 8 minutes at 180°C.

items.name: Liège Waffles
items.desc: Plan to let the dough rest in the fridge overnight for light, flavourful waffles.
steps: Place the milk, yeast, cane sugar and 1 cup of flour in a bowl and mix into a soft dough with an electric mixer. Let rest for about 15 minutes.

Whisk together the eggs, maple syrup or honey, butter and vanilla. Add to the dough with the remaining flour and salt, and mix into a soft, sticky dough. Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour.
Punch down the dough and scrape it from the sides. Loosely cover and rest in the fridge overnight.
Divide the dough into 12 portions, shape into balls and roll in pearled sugar. Wrap individually (they can be frozen at this point).
Heat the waffle iron, press the dough on and cook until golden and crisp.

items.name: Orange Yoghurt Cake
steps: Prepare a 20cm cake tin or loaf tin.
Cream the butter, orange rind and sugar until light and fluffy, then beat in the egg yolks one at a time.
Add half the sifted flour with half the yoghurt and half the orange juice; mix well, then repeat with the rest.
Beat the egg whites to soft peaks.
Fold a third of the egg whites into the batter to lighten it, then fold in the rest very lightly.
Bake at 160°C for about 1 hour.

items.name: Queen Cakes
steps: Cream the butter and sugar, beat in the eggs one at a time, sift in the flour and baking powder, then add the sultanas.
Put the mixture into greased patty tins (makes 21).
Bake for 10–12 minutes at 200°C.

items.name: Upside-Down Plum Cake
ingredients: Topping: ½ teaspoon fresh lime juice
Topping: 4 prune plums, not peeled, cut into 6 wedges each
Batter: pinch of freshly grated nutmeg
Batter: ½ cup butter, at room temperature
steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C.
Pour the melted butter into a 10-inch cake pan and swirl to coat the inside.
Sprinkle the brown sugar over, arrange the plum wedges in a single layer and drizzle with lime juice. Set aside.
Sift together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, nutmeg and cinnamon and set aside.
Cream the butter and sugar until light and fluffy, then add the eggs and beat until smooth.
Alternating, add a third of the dry ingredients and a third of the milk, beating between additions, then beat for 1 minute.
Pour the batter over the plum wedges and bake for about 60 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the pan on a wire rack for 30 minutes, then invert onto a plate to serve.

items.name: Easy Pad Thai
ingredients: 1 cup finely chopped cooked chicken, cooked pork and/or prawns
¾ cup loosely packed coriander leaves
steps: Soak the noodles in hot water for around 15 minutes or until soft, rinse in cold water, drain and set aside.
Heat the oil in a wok or large fry pan and cook the garlic and shallots for a minute, taking care not to burn.
Add the egg and allow to set for a minute, stir, then add the noodles, prawns and meat and toss to combine.
Add the fish sauce, lime juice and palm sugar and stir to mix.
Add the peanuts and sprouts, heat through, then transfer to a serving dish.
Sprinkle with coriander, drizzle with sweet chilli sauce and serve with lime wedges.

items.name: Famous Brade Green Chicken Curry
ingredients: Rubbed mint & rubbed basil (a lot — about a tablespoon)
Green curry paste, about a tablespoon (e.g. Masterfoods)
1 can coconut cream and 1 can coconut milk
Peas, as many as you like
steps: Brown the chicken and onion in a pan.
Add the rubbed mint and rubbed basil (use plenty for the flavour, about a tablespoon).
Add the green curry paste, about a tablespoon.
Add the coconut cream and coconut milk.
Add the peas.
Let it simmer for a while, then add brown sugar to taste — the more you add, the milder the heat.

items.name: Jesse's Garlic Chicken Thighs
steps: Heat oil in a pan or tagine.
Sauté the garlic, onion, chilli, salt and pepper.
Once the onion is softened, lightly brown the chicken thighs.
Add the chicken stock and slowly reduce down (approx half).
Add the powdered chicken soup and mix.
Slowly add the evaporated milk so it doesn't split.
Reduce the heat, put the lid on and cook a further 15 minutes.
A few minutes before serving, add green beans or chopped bok choy.
Serve with rice.

items.name: Shane's Ribs
items.desc: Made up from a few recipes, but it went something like this.
ingredients: ½ a dried chilli, all ground up
½ cup Whitlock's smoky BBQ sauce
steps: Mix everything (except the ribs) over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Put the ribs and sauce in a slow cooker and mix.
Cook on low for 8 hours.
Remove the ribs, reduce the sauce in a pot until thick, then pour over the ribs.

items.name: Lamb Shanks
steps: Coat the lamb shanks in flour and brown in a pan.
Add the garlic, balsamic vinegar, tomatoes, beef stock and herbs.
Bring the mixture to the boil.
Put the shanks in an oven dish and pour the mixture over.
Bake at 180°C for 2 hours.

items.name: Slow-Cooked Chicken Noodle Soup
steps: Add the potatoes, carrots, onion, garlic, stock, soup and chicken thighs to the slow cooker and cook until tender.
Once cooked and ready to serve, cook the noodles and add them into the soup.

items.name: Mussels
steps: Heat the wine, spring onion, garlic and butter in a pot.
Add the rinsed and scrubbed mussels and cook covered for 5 minutes, until the shells open.

items.name: BBQ Prawns
steps: Marinate the prawns in the fridge for at least an hour.
Put on the BBQ, turning only once.
Cook until golden brown.

items.name: Sticky Date Pudding
steps: Cook the dates in the water.
Beat in the butter and remaining pudding ingredients.
Pour into a tin and bake at 190°C for 25 minutes.
For the sauce, place all the sauce ingredients in a pot, bring to the boil stirring, and boil for 5 minutes.
Cover the pudding with the hot sauce.

items.name: Chocolate Self-Saucing Pudding
items.desc: A Clements family dessert since the early 1980s — adapted from the Edmonds cookbook. Doubles well for a crowd.
ingredients: Water or milk, as required for a thick batter
Sauce: ½ cup (125 ml) brown sugar
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line a 1.5–2L ovenproof dish with baking paper, or grease it.
Beat together the white sugar, softened butter, egg and vanilla.
Sift the flour, baking powder and cocoa together, then fold into the beaten mixture, adding water or milk as needed for a thick cake batter.
Spoon the mixture into the dish.
Sprinkle over the brown sugar, cocoa and cornflour, then gently pour the boiling water over the back of a spoon to make the sauce.
Bake at 180°C for 35 minutes, or until cooked through (try covering two-thirds of the dish with a lid).

items.name: Tiramisu
items.desc: Coffee-soaked sponge fingers layered with creamy mascarpone and dusted with dark cocoa.
ingredients: 3 tbsp dark cocoa powder, for dusting
steps: Bring a medium pot of water to a simmer and set aside a square serving dish (about 20 x 20cm).
Place the egg yolks and caster sugar in a large heatproof bowl that will sit over the pot without touching the water.
Set the bowl over the pot and whisk continuously for about 10 minutes, until light and fluffy. Remove and cool for 2 minutes.
Whisk the mascarpone into the cooled egg mixture.
In a separate bowl, whisk the cream and vanilla to stiff peaks, then gently fold into the mascarpone mixture.
Briefly dip the biscuits in the espresso and arrange in a single layer in the dish.
Spread over half the mascarpone mixture, repeat with a second layer of biscuits and mascarpone, and dust with cocoa.
Chill for at least 3 hours, ideally overnight. Don't let the biscuits get too soggy when dipping.

items.name: Pumpkin Pie
ingredients: 1¼ cups half and half (or whole milk)
steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Place the pumpkin in a bowl, add the melted butter and stir well.
In a separate bowl, beat the eggs well, then beat in the milk, brown sugar, salt and spices until blended. Add the pumpkin mixture and mix well.
Pour into the pie shell and bake at 220°C for 10 minutes.
Reduce the heat to 175°C and bake a further 30–40 minutes, until the filling is firm.
Cool and serve with whipped cream.

items.name: Caramel Banana
items.desc: Warm caramelised banana spooned over vanilla ice cream.
steps: Pre-heat a frying pan on a gentle temperature and slice the bananas.
Melt some butter, then add liberal amounts of brown sugar. As the sugar starts to melt, add the banana.
Stir slowly to let the banana soften the sugar. Once melted into a caramel sauce, spoon the banana and sauce over vanilla ice cream.

items.name: Creamy Mushrooms
steps: Heat the butter, then add the mushrooms and garlic and cook until soft.
Turn the heat up high, add the cream and bring to the boil.
Wait until the cream has thickened. Nice with parmesan stirred through.

items.name: Turkish Flatbread
ingredients: A few tsp each of sesame seeds and black cumin seeds, for sprinkling
steps: Place the flour, yeast and salt in a large bowl and stir to mix.
Add the water bit by bit, mixing to a very soft, almost sloppy dough — thicker than sponge cake mixture but softer than usual bread dough.
Cover with a tea towel and rise in a warm place for about 1 hour. Preheat the oven to 250°C with a large baking tray on the middle rack.
Remove the hot tray, sprinkle with flour, scrape the dough onto it and gently press into shape, pushing your fingers in a few times.
Spray or brush with a mix of cold water and a dash of olive oil, then sprinkle with the seeds.
Bake for about 12 minutes, brush/spray again, then bake a further 5–8 minutes until golden.
Wrap the hot bread tightly in a tea towel to keep a soft crust, then serve in chunks or split and stuffed.
